definitionEn: to formally end a law, custom or system so that it no longer exists
situation: An authority decides that a rule, fee, institution or tradition will officially stop existing.

examples.text: The city [[abolished]] bus fares last year, and now everyone travels for free.
Our company has [[abolished]] fixed working hours, so staff can start and finish whenever they like.
Reformers campaigned for decades to [[abolish]] the practice of sending young children to work in factories.

texts: Many people would love to [[abolish]] the annual switch to summer time.
The university plans to [[abolish]] entrance exams and select students by interview instead.
If you could [[abolish]] one rule in this office, which would it be?

badCollocation.noteRu: Решение суда или начальства не abolish, а overturn или reverse. Abolish — упразднить закон, налог или систему целиком.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Монархию, налоги и законы упраздняют глаголом abolish. Cancel — про встречи и заказы, resign — уйти в отставку, delete — удалить файл.

nuance.text: The council voted to [[abolish]] parking charges in the town centre.
nuance.explanationRu: Abolish — официально упразднить сбор, правило или систему. Demolish — снести здание; парковочные сборы снести нельзя.

reverse.text: The old cinema was [[demolished]] to make room for new flats.
reverse.explanationRu: Здания сносят — demolish. Abolish относится к законам, налогам и обычаям, а не к постройкам.

fixIt.text: The reform [[liquidated]] three ministries and merged their work into a single department.
fixIt.explanationRu: Liquidate по-английски — ликвидировать фирму через продажу её активов. Министерства и должности упраздняют — abolish.

wordFormation.text: The [[abolition]] of roaming charges made calling home from abroad much cheaper.

reply.context: A colleague messages you: "Big news: management wants to scrap the dress code completely."
options: Kindly be advised that I concur with the abolition of said code.
About time! Nobody follows it anyway, so they might as well abolish it.
Great, maybe they'll abolish my old laptop too, it's so slow.
reply.explanationRu: Abolish подходит к правилам и системам, а не к вещам вроде ноутбука. Первый вариант звучит как канцелярское письмо, а не ответ коллеге в чате.

definitionEn: the fact that something is lacking or does not exist
senseNote: Выбрано значение «отсутствие чего-либо» (absence of evidence); значение «неявка на работу или в школу» не тренируется.
situation: You notice that something expected, such as proof, interest or a clear rule, simply is not there.

examples.text: In the [[absence]] of any clear evidence, the court had no choice but to release him.
What worried investors most was the complete [[absence]] of a long-term plan.
Dinner with his parents was polite enough, but there was a striking [[absence]] of warmth.

texts: The [[absence]] of street lights makes this road dangerous at night.
Doctors were puzzled by the [[absence]] of any obvious symptoms.
Silence is not simply the [[absence]] of noise; it can feel full of meaning.

badCollocation.noteRu: О нехватке времени или денег говорят lack of time или no time. Absence звучит книжно и подходит к доказательствам, объяснениям, правилам.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Идиома conspicuous by its absence — «бросается в глаза своим отсутствием». Lack, shortage и loss в эту фразу не входят.

nuance.text: In the [[absence]] of clear instructions, the team decided to wait.
nuance.explanationRu: In the absence of — устойчивая модель «при отсутствии». С lack так не говорят: нужно for lack of или without.

reverse.text: She was exhausted from [[lack]] of sleep after the night shift.
reverse.explanationRu: Нехватку сна, денег, времени обозначают словом lack. Absence of sleep звучит неестественно: absence — полное отсутствие, а не нехватка.

fixIt.text: The [[deficit]] of any explanation from the airline made passengers even angrier.
fixIt.explanationRu: Deficit — дефицит бюджета или торговли. Когда чего-то просто нет (объяснений, доказательств), говорят absence.

wordFormation.text: The [[absence]] of a clear timetable made planning the trip almost impossible.

reply.context: In a meeting, your manager asks: "Why do you think the project stalled last spring?"
options: Honestly, a total absence of time — everyone was far too busy.
Be advised that the absence of leadership is hereby cited as the primary cause.
Mostly the absence of a clear leader: nobody felt able to make decisions.
reply.explanationRu: Absence — полное отсутствие (лидера, плана); о нехватке времени говорят lack of time. Второй ответ звучит как казённый документ, а не живой разговор.

rewrite.original: Because there was no reliable data, the team had to guess.
rewrite.frame: In ____ reliable data, the team had to guess.
rewrite.explanationRu: Устойчивое выражение: in the absence of — «при отсутствии».

definitionEn: not present or not found in a place, situation or thing
senseNote: Выбрано значение «отсутствует там, где его ожидаешь» (humour is absent from the film); «не пришёл на урок или работу» не тренируется.
situation: You point out that a quality, feature or element you expected cannot be found anywhere in something.

examples.text: In the sequel, the sharp humour of her first novel is almost entirely [[absent]], and the jokes feel forced.
Large predators are now [[absent]] across much of the region, so deer numbers have soared.
She read out the results in a flat, calm voice; any hint of emotion was completely [[absent]].

texts: Vitamin D is naturally [[absent]] from most everyday foods.
Women were largely [[absent]] from the history books we studied at school.
In his letters, any warmth towards his brother is strangely [[absent]].

badCollocation.noteRu: Конструкции absent of нет. Говорят humour is absent from the film или the film is devoid of humour.

collocationTask.explanationRu: После absent нужен предлог from: absent from the discussion. Предлоги of, to и by с этим прилагательным не сочетаются.

nuance.text: Humour is completely [[absent]] from his latest novel.
nuance.explanationRu: Absent from — «отсутствует в чём-то» (юмор в книге, факты в отчёте). Away говорят только о людях, которые уехали или не на месте.

reverse.text: Sorry, my manager is [[away]] until Monday — can I take a message?
reverse.explanationRu: О коллеге в отпуске или командировке говорят away. Absent в такой фразе звучит как отметка о прогуле в журнале.

fixIt.text: Clear instructions were completely [[absence]] from the manual that came with the printer.
fixIt.explanationRu: После were нужно прилагательное: absent from — «отсутствует». Absence — существительное «отсутствие».

wordFormation.text: She stirred her coffee [[absently]], her mind clearly somewhere else.

rewrite.original: The new model has none of the features that made the old one popular.
rewrite.frame: The features that made the old model popular ____ from the new one.
rewrite.explanationRu: Absent from — «отсутствуют в чём-то»; перед прилагательным нужен глагол are.

definitionEn: completely unreasonable or ridiculous, making no sense at all
situation: You react to an idea, rule, price or claim that seems ridiculous and completely unreasonable.

examples.text: Asking the team to finish a six-month project in two weeks is simply [[absurd]].
Twelve euros for a coffee? That's an [[absurd]] price, even for an airport.
The play's plot is deliberately [[absurd]]: a man wakes up to find he has turned into a chair.

texts: It seems [[absurd]] to pay rent for a flat we never use.
The rumour that the boss sleeps in his office is clearly [[absurd]].
Looking back, our whole argument about the parking space was [[absurd]].

badCollocation.noteRu: Absurd — уже сильное слово, поэтому его усиливают словами completely, utterly или simply, а не very.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Absurd усиливают наречиями utterly, completely, patently. Strongly, greatly и heavily с этим прилагательным не сочетаются.

nuance.text: Charging customers for a glass of tap water is [[absurd]].
nuance.explanationRu: Absurd — нелепый, лишённый логики (правило, цена, требование). Surreal — странный, как во сне; о плате за воду так не говорят.

reverse.text: Meeting my childhood hero in a supermarket queue felt completely [[surreal]].
reverse.explanationRu: Surreal — «как во сне, нереально». Absurd значило бы «нелепо, глупо», а встреча с кумиром скорее невероятна, чем глупа.

fixIt.text: The situation became so [[anecdotal]] that even the manager started laughing.
fixIt.explanationRu: Anecdotal значит «основанный на отдельных историях» (anecdotal evidence). Нелепая, смехотворная ситуация — absurd.

wordFormation.text: Everyone could see the [[absurdity]] of holding a meeting to plan another meeting.

reply.context: A colleague sighs: "They want the full report by tomorrow morning, and we only got the data an hour ago."
options: How absurd! I'm really looking forward to reading it.
One must pronounce such a request absurd in the extreme, madam.
That's absurd — nobody could write it properly in one evening.
reply.explanationRu: Absurd — «нелепо, так не бывает», это возмущение, а не радость. Вариант с madam звучит театрально и не подходит для разговора с коллегой.

definitionEn: a very large amount of something, often more than enough
situation: You describe a place, season or source where there is much more of something than people need.

examples.text: Locals love the island for its [[abundance]] of fresh fish and seafood.
Wild mushrooms grow here in [[abundance]] every autumn, so bring a big basket.
In a world of information [[abundance]], the real challenge is deciding what to ignore.

texts: This year's [[abundance]] of tomatoes meant we gave half of them away.
Despite the [[abundance]] of cheap flights, many people still prefer the train.
The city is famous for its [[abundance]] of parks and green spaces.

badCollocation.noteRu: О толпе не говорят abundance of people — скажите crowds of people или a lot of people. Abundance — об изобилии ресурсов, еды, возможностей.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Устойчивое выражение in abundance — «в изобилии». Majority, amount и richness в эту модель не встают.

nuance.text: Children growing up in the countryside enjoy an [[abundance]] of fresh air and space.
nuance.explanationRu: Abundance — изобилие чего-то хорошего и нужного. Excess — излишек, «слишком много», это звучит как проблема, а свежий воздух проблемой не бывает.

reverse.text: The doctor warned him that an [[excess]] of salt was raising his blood pressure.
reverse.explanationRu: Когда чего-то слишком много и это вредно (соль, сахар), говорят excess. Abundance звучит положительно.

fixIt.text: The rainforest is famous for its [[affluence]] of plant and insect species.
fixIt.explanationRu: Affluence — достаток, богатство людей (affluent families). Изобилие видов, ресурсов, еды — abundance.

wordFormation.text: Tourists are drawn by the [[abundance]] of cheap, delicious street food.

rewrite.original: Wild strawberries grow everywhere in this forest, in huge numbers.
rewrite.frame: Wild strawberries grow ____ in this forest.
rewrite.explanationRu: In abundance — «в изобилии», устойчивое выражение без артикля.

definitionEn: the wrong or harmful use of something, such as power, drugs or trust
senseNote: Выбрано значение «злоупотребление» (abuse of power, drug abuse); значения «жестокое обращение» и «оскорбления» не тренируются.
situation: Someone uses their position, a privilege, a substance or a system in a harmful or dishonest way.

examples.text: The accountant who secretly moved clients' savings into her own account committed a gross [[abuse]] of trust.
Years of alcohol [[abuse]] had seriously damaged his liver.
Free trials are limited to one per customer to prevent [[abuse]] of the system.

texts: The charity runs programmes to prevent drug [[abuse]] in schools.
Critics warned that the new benefit system was wide open to [[abuse]].
Strict rules on expense claims are meant to stop [[abuse]] by a few employees.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Злоупотреблять сладким» — eat too many sweets или overdo the sweets. Abuse звучит как серьёзная зависимость или преступное злоупотребление.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Злоупотребление властью — an abuse of power. Excess — «избыток», overdose — «передозировка», insult — «оскорбление»; с power так не говорят.

nuance.text: Using public money to redecorate his own home was a clear [[abuse]] of his position.
nuance.explanationRu: Abuse of position или power — использовать должность или власть ради личной выгоды. Violation — нарушение правил или прав; «нарушить должность» нельзя.

reverse.text: Filming people without their consent is a [[violation]] of privacy.
reverse.explanationRu: Нарушение права или правила — violation of privacy или of the rules. С privacy слово abuse не сочетается: его берут с power, trust, position.

fixIt.text: The mayor was accused of an [[overuse]] of power after giving city jobs to his relatives.
fixIt.explanationRu: Злоупотребление властью — abuse of power. Overuse — «слишком частое использование» (overuse of antibiotics), а не корыстное.

wordFormation.text: Regulators fined the bank for [[abusive]] lending practices that trapped customers in debt.

reply.context: In a team chat, someone asks: "Should we let everyone use the company card for taxis?"
options: Only with receipts — otherwise the system is open to abuse.
Sure, and let's abuse the drivers with huge tips.
Verily, such generosity doth invite abuse most grievous.
reply.explanationRu: Open to abuse — «открыт для злоупотреблений». Abuse the drivers значит «оскорблять водителей», а третий ответ звучит как пьеса Шекспира.

definitionEn: an official society of distinguished scientists, scholars or artists that promotes their field
senseNote: Выбрано значение «академия как объединение учёных или деятелей искусства» (academy of sciences); значение «специальное училище» (police academy) не тренируется.
situation: You talk about the official body that elects top scientists or artists as members and honours their work.

examples.text: At forty-two, she became the youngest scientist ever elected to the national [[academy]].
Every summer the [[academy]] invites its members to exhibit their latest paintings and sculptures.
The language [[academy]] has officially accepted several new words borrowed from English.

texts: Only a handful of women were elected to the [[academy]] in its first century.
The [[academy]] publishes an official dictionary every few decades.
His paintings were rejected by the [[academy]], so he organised his own exhibition.

badCollocation.noteRu: Академия наук — сообщество учёных: в неё избирают (be elected to), а не оканчивают её, как вуз.

collocationTask.explanationRu: В академию как сообщество учёных избирают — be elected to the academy. Enrolled — о студентах, hired — о сотрудниках, graduated — об окончании вуза.

nuance.text: Last year the [[academy]] elected twelve new members, including two physicists.
nuance.explanationRu: Academy — конкретная организация с членами и выборами. Academia — весь мир университетов и науки в целом; он никого не избирает.

reverse.text: After ten years in [[academia]], she moved into industry.
reverse.explanationRu: Academia — академическая среда, мир вузов и исследований. Academy — конкретная организация, и in academy так не говорят.

fixIt.text: The national [[academic]] of sciences has awarded her its highest medal.
fixIt.explanationRu: Academic — учёный или прилагательное «академический». Организация, в которую избирают учёных, — academy.

reply.context: A colleague mentions: "My old professor has just been elected to the academy of sciences."
options: That's a huge honour — the academy only elects a few people each year.
Great! Will she be taking classes at the academy from September?
Kindly convey my most profound felicitations upon her elevation to the academy.
reply.explanationRu: В академию наук избирают за научные заслуги, там не ходят на занятия. Третий вариант звучит слишком торжественно для разговора с коллегой.

definitionEn: to make a process or change happen faster or sooner
senseNote: Выбрано значение «ускорять процесс, развитие»; значение «набирать скорость (о машине)» не тренируется.
situation: A change, trend or project starts moving faster, often because of a new policy, event or technology.

examples.text: The pandemic [[accelerated]] the shift to online shopping, squeezing ten years of change into one.
Hiring two more developers should [[accelerate]] the project and help us meet the deadline.
Reading widely is one of the best ways of [[accelerating]] your progress in a new language.

texts: Rising temperatures [[accelerate]] the melting of mountain glaciers.
New software tools can [[accelerate]] the design process dramatically.
Some parents try to [[accelerate]] their children's learning with extra classes.

badCollocation.noteRu: Встречу на более раннее время переносят — bring forward или move up. Accelerate — ускорить процесс или рост, а не сдвинуть дату.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Рост экономики ускоряют — accelerate economic growth. Hurry, hustle и race — о спешке людей, с экономическим ростом они не сочетаются.

nuance.text: The government wants to [[accelerate]] the switch to electric buses.
nuance.explanationRu: Accelerate — ускорить процесс, рост, переход. Hurry — «спешить, торопиться» о людях; hurry the switch звучит неестественно.

reverse.text: Please [[hurry]] — the taxi is already waiting outside.
reverse.explanationRu: Человеку, который опаздывает, говорят hurry. Accelerate — о процессах и машинах, а не о сборах к такси.

fixIt.text: Working with a good mentor can [[fasten]] your career development more than any online course.
fixIt.explanationRu: Fasten — «застегнуть, пристегнуть» (fasten your seatbelt). Ускорить развитие или процесс — accelerate.

wordFormation.text: The sudden [[acceleration]] of inflation took many economists by surprise.

reply.context: In a meeting, your manager asks: "How can we get the new app to market sooner?"
options: We could accelerate testing by bringing in an outside team.
We could accelerate the budget by cutting a few costs.
Just floor it, mate, and chuck the thing out already.
reply.explanationRu: Accelerate сочетается с процессами (testing, growth), а «ускорить бюджет» бессмысленно. Третий ответ слишком грубый и разговорный для совещания.

rewrite.original: The new policy made the move to renewable energy happen faster.
rewrite.frame: The new policy ____ the move to renewable energy.
rewrite.explanationRu: Make something happen faster — то же, что accelerate something: «ускорить».

definitionEn: the general agreement that an idea, product or person is suitable or welcome
senseNote: Выбрано значение «признание, одобрение обществом» (gain acceptance); значение «согласие принять предложение или приглашение» не тренируется.
situation: Over time, more and more people come to see a new idea, product or group as normal and welcome.

examples.text: It took decades for the theory of continental drift to gain wide [[acceptance]] among scientists.
For many immigrants, learning the language is the first step towards [[acceptance]] in their new community.
Remote work, once seen as a risky experiment, now enjoys broad [[acceptance]] among employers.

texts: Public [[acceptance]] of self-driving cars is still surprisingly low.
Her poetry finally found [[acceptance]] after years of rejection by critics.
The campaign aims to promote [[acceptance]] of people with different body shapes.

badCollocation.noteRu: Признание заслуг и таланта — recognition. Acceptance — готовность считать что-то нормальным или правильным.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Признание завоёвывают: gain или win acceptance. Make, do и take с acceptance не сочетаются.

nuance.text: It took years for online banking to win general [[acceptance]] among older customers.
nuance.explanationRu: Acceptance — люди начинают считать что-то нормальным и пользоваться этим. Recognition — признание заслуг; к онлайн-банку у пожилых клиентов это не подходит.

reverse.text: She received international [[recognition]] for her work on malaria.
reverse.explanationRu: Признание заслуг учёного — recognition. Acceptance значит «одобрение, готовность принять», за работу его не получают.

fixIt.text: The idea of a four-day week is slowly gaining [[admission]] among employers.
fixIt.explanationRu: Admission — «признание вины» или «приём, вход». Когда идею постепенно начинают одобрять, говорят gain acceptance.

wordFormation.text: The film explores a teenager's struggle for [[acceptance]] at a new school.

reply.context: At a debate club, someone asks: "Do you think electric cars will ever replace petrol ones?"
options: Probably, but most drivers haven't sent their acceptance yet.
Probably. They've already gained wide acceptance in several countries.
Totes, they're like sooo accepted now, no cap.
reply.explanationRu: Gain acceptance — «получить признание, стать привычным». Send acceptance — ответ на приглашение, здесь не к месту. Третий вариант — сленг, для дебатов не годится.

definitionEn: easy for people without special knowledge to understand or enjoy
senseNote: Выбрано значение «понятный, доступный для понимания» (an accessible book); значение «такой, куда можно попасть» не тренируется.
situation: A book, talk, artwork or explanation is made so that people without special training can follow it.

examples.text: Her brilliant book makes quantum physics [[accessible]] to readers with no scientific background.
The museum keeps its exhibitions [[accessible]] by avoiding long academic texts on the walls.
I know you don't like jazz, but this album is really [[accessible]], so give it a try.

texts: The lecturer has a gift for making complex ideas [[accessible]].
Written in plain language, the report is [[accessible]] to any interested reader.
Opera can be surprisingly [[accessible]] if you start with the popular classics.

badCollocation.noteRu: Доступная цена — affordable price. Accessible — «понятный» или «такой, куда можно попасть», но не «недорогой».

collocationTask.explanationRu: Понятное, доходчивое введение — an accessible introduction. Available — «имеющийся в наличии», achievable — «достижимый», admissible — «допустимый».

nuance.text: The textbook explains statistics in a clear, [[accessible]] way.
nuance.explanationRu: Accessible — понятный без специальной подготовки. Available — «есть в наличии, можно получить»; манера объяснения не бывает available.

reverse.text: Tickets for the festival are [[available]] online from Monday.
reverse.explanationRu: О билетах и товарах, которые можно купить, говорят available. Accessible означало бы «понятные» или «куда можно пройти».

fixIt.text: Good popular science books make difficult ideas [[reachable]] to ordinary readers.
fixIt.explanationRu: Reachable — «до чего можно добраться или дозвониться». Идеи, понятные обычному читателю, — accessible.

wordFormation.text: Critics praised the [[accessibility]] of her writing, which never talks down to readers.

reply.context: A friend texts: "Can you recommend a book about economics? I'm a total beginner."
options: I would humbly submit that this volume is eminently accessible to the uninitiated.
Try this one — it's very accessible, only five pounds in most shops.
Try this one — it's really accessible and there's hardly any maths.
reply.explanationRu: Accessible — «понятный новичку». О низкой цене говорят affordable или cheap. Первый ответ звучит слишком книжно для переписки с другом.
